court: Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm Article III and statutory jurisdiction over the habeas and class claims on remand.

issues.label: §1252(f)(1) scope
issues.why: The court must decide whether 8 U.S.C. §1252(f)(1) bars class-wide declaratory relief (not just injunctions) affecting §1226(a).

issues.label: §1252(a)(5) channeling
issues.why: The court must consider whether any claims are impermissibly channeled to petitions for review rather than district court.

issues.label: §1252(b)(9) consolidation
issues.why: The court must determine whether claims arise from removal proceedings such that §1252(b)(9) strips district-court jurisdiction.

issues.label: §1252(d) exhaustion limits
issues.why: The court must consider any statutory exhaustion requirements and whether they apply to constitutional/procedural bond-hearing claims.

issues.label: Habeas jurisdiction preserved
issues.why: The court must assess whether habeas jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. §2241 remains available for detention-procedure challenges.

issues.label: Sovereign immunity waiver
issues.why: The court must confirm a proper cause of action/waiver (e.g., habeas/APA-equivalent) for the declaratory relief sought against federal officials.

issues.label: Proper defendants
issues.why: The court must ensure the named federal officials/agencies are proper parties for the relief requested.

issues.label: Mootness of named plaintiff
issues.why: Because Onosamba-Ohindo was released, the court must determine if his individual claims are moot.

issues.label: Inherently transitory exception
issues.why: The court must decide whether the class claims evade review such that class claims remain live despite the representative’s release.

issues.label: Relation-back doctrine
issues.why: The court must decide whether class certification/claims relate back to filing/certification to avoid mootness.

issues.label: Live controversy for class
issues.why: The court must determine whether there remains a live dispute given changed agency practices and the end of the injunction.

issues.label: Voluntary cessation
issues.why: If the government changed bond-hearing practices, the court must decide whether cessation moots the case or could recur.

issues.label: Ripeness
issues.why: For pre-hearing detainees, the court must confirm the dispute is fit for review and not speculative.

issues.label: Standing—injury in fact
issues.why: The court must assess whether class members face a real and imminent procedural injury under current bond-hearing practices.

issues.label: Standing—traceability
issues.why: The court must determine whether alleged due-process harms are fairly traceable to defendants’ policies (IJ/BIA framework).

issues.label: Standing—redressability
issues.why: The court must decide whether a declaratory judgment would likely redress the harms, given EOIR/IJ decisionmaking.

issues.label: Advisory opinion concern
issues.why: The court must ensure the requested declaration would resolve a concrete dispute rather than provide abstract guidance.

issues.label: Declaratory Judgment Act discretion
issues.why: Even with jurisdiction, the court must decide whether declaratory relief is appropriate and useful under 28 U.S.C. §2201.

issues.label: Declaratory vs injunctive relief
issues.why: The court must decide whether the requested declaration is functionally equivalent to an injunction barred by §1252(f)(1).

issues.label: Rule 23(a) prerequisites
issues.why: The court must reassess numerosity, commonality, typicality, and adequacy for the Pre-Hearing Class.

issues.label: Rule 23(b)(2) fit
issues.why: The court must decide whether declaratory relief is truly “indivisible” and appropriate for class-wide treatment post-Aleman Gonzalez.

issues.label: Need for individualized inquiries
issues.why: The court must decide whether ability-to-pay/alternatives and prejudice require individualized determinations defeating (b)(2).

issues.label: Class definition ascertainability
issues.why: The court must ensure the class is defined by objective criteria (detained under §1226(a) at BFFDF, pre-hearing).

issues.label: Geographic/venue limits
issues.why: The court must confirm the class limited to Buffalo Federal Detention Facility/Batavia-Buffalo courts is proper and manageable.

issues.label: Adequacy after release
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether a released representative can adequately represent currently detained class members.

issues.label: Class counsel adequacy
issues.why: The court must confirm appointed counsel can fairly and adequately represent the class.

issues.label: Decertification standard
issues.why: The court must apply the correct legal standard and burden for decertifying an already-certified class.

issues.label: Effect of remedy unavailability
issues.why: The court must decide whether loss of class-wide injunctive relief alone justifies decertification under Rule 23(b)(2).

issues.label: Summary judgment justiciability
issues.why: The court must decide whether summary judgment is moot or still presents a live claim for declaratory relief.

issues.label: Rule 12(b)(1) dismissal grounds
issues.why: The court must identify any jurisdictional defects (mootness, standing, §1252) supporting dismissal.

issues.label: Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal grounds
issues.why: The court must decide whether the complaint states a plausible due process claim for the procedures requested.

issues.label: Standard of review on motions
issues.why: The court must apply correct standards for summary judgment, decertification, and dismissal on the current record.

issues.label: Due process liberty interest
issues.why: The court must determine the nature/weight of the detainee’s liberty interest under §1226(a) custody redeterminations.

issues.label: Mathews v. Eldridge balancing
issues.why: The court must apply Mathews to assess what procedures due process requires at §1226(a) bond hearings.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process permits placing the burden on the noncitizen (Matter of Guerra) or requires the government to bear it.

issues.label: Burden standard level
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process requires clear and convincing evidence, preponderance, or another standard.

issues.label: Danger/flight-risk criteria
issues.why: The court must determine what substantive findings are constitutionally required (danger, flight risk) to justify detention.

issues.label: Least-restrictive conditions finding
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process requires a finding that no condition/combination of conditions can assure appearance/safety.

issues.label: Consideration of alternatives
issues.why: The court must decide whether IJs must consider non-bond alternatives (supervision, reporting, etc.) as a constitutional requirement.

issues.label: Ability-to-pay consideration
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process requires considering ability to pay when setting bond to avoid wealth-based detention.

issues.label: Procedural safeguards content
issues.why: The court must decide whether due process requires specific procedures (evidence rules, record, findings) beyond burden/standard issues.

issues.label: Role of BIA precedents
issues.why: The court must assess how Matter of Guerra/Barreiros interact with constitutional requirements and whether courts can override them.

issues.label: Deference to agency interpretation
issues.why: The court must decide what, if any, deference is owed to DHS/EOIR/BIA interpretations of §1226(a) and regulations in this context.

issues.label: Statutory-avoidance canon
issues.why: The court must consider whether to construe §1226(a)/regulations to avoid constitutional problems rather than reach constitutional questions.

issues.label: Regulatory authority limits
issues.why: The court must determine whether current regulations (8 C.F.R. §§236.1, 1003.19, 1236.1) permit/forbid the requested procedures.

issues.label: Separation-of-powers constraints
issues.why: The court must ensure the relief would not impermissibly direct how IJs adjudicate in a manner beyond judicial power.

issues.label: Practical enforceability of declaration
issues.why: The court must assess whether a declaration would have concrete operative effect on future bond hearings despite §1252(f)(1).

issues.label: Scope of declaratory relief
issues.why: The court must tailor any declaration to avoid overbreadth and to match the certified class and proven practices.

issues.label: Temporal scope on remand
issues.why: The court must determine whether claims cover practices during the injunction period, after it ended, or both.

issues.label: Effect of prior injunction compliance
issues.why: The court must decide whether past compliance affects liability, mootness, or the need for declaratory relief.

issues.label: Collateral consequences
issues.why: The court must consider whether class members suffer ongoing consequences (e.g., continued detention) that keep claims live.

issues.label: Prejudice requirement relevance
issues.why: The court must decide whether class-wide relief requires showing class members were prejudiced by the challenged procedures.

issues.label: Record adequacy for class relief
issues.why: The court must determine whether there is sufficient evidence of a uniform policy/practice to support class-wide declaratory relief.

issues.label: Remand mandate adherence
issues.why: The court must ensure its rulings comply with the appellate remand scope and any law-of-the-case principles.
